issues.legal_issue: A nominee appointed to decide a cooperative-society dispute is not a court for the purpose of the restriction on taking cognizance of document-forgery offences.
material_facts: A dispute about membership and participation in a society’s meeting was referred by the Registrar to a nominee for adjudication.
The accused were alleged to have forged a society’s minutes and produced the document in the proceeding before the nominee.
The nominee was appointed by the Registrar, whose authority over the proceeding included the power to withdraw the dispute and appoint another decision-maker.
issues.conclusion: The nominee was not a court for the purpose of section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, so a complaint by the nominee or a court to which the nominee was subordinate was not required for the Magistrate to take cognizance.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 195(1)(c) and 195(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the specified document-related offences require a complaint by the relevant court only when committed in the circumstances stated in the provision. A body’s obligation to act fairly and impartially, its power to hear evidence and decide disputes, and the effect of its decisions do not by themselves make it a court; the nominee’s authority arose from the Registrar’s appointment and remained subject to the Registrar’s control, making the nominee substantially an arbitrator. The Court considered, among other authorities, Shri Virindar Kumar Satyawadi v. State of Punjab, Brajnandan Sinha v. Jyoti Narain, Jagannath Prasad v. State of Uttar Pradesh, Lalji Haridas v. State of Maharashtra, and Thakur Jugal Kishore Sinha v. Sitamarhi Central Co-operative Bank Ltd.

predicates.criminal_prosecution_for_forgery_of_docu: A criminal prosecution alleges forgery of a document produced or given in evidence in an earlier dispute proceeding.
predicates.prior_decider_is_registrar_nominee: The person who decided the earlier dispute was appointed as a nominee by a registrar.
predicates.nominee_authority_is_personal_and_withdr: The nominee’s authority to decide the dispute came from an appointment by the registrar, who could withdraw the dispute or appoint another decision-maker.

issues.definition: When a forgery prosecution concerns a document used in a dispute proceeding decided by a registrar’s nominee whose authority is appointed and withdrawable, the nominee is not treated as a court for the document-offence complaint bar.

issues.legal_issue: An offence concerning falsification of cooperative-society records does not repeal the general criminal offences of forgery merely because some conduct may fall within both sets of offences.
material_facts: The complaint alleged that society officers dishonestly altered the society’s minutes to make it appear that a resolution had included a clause that was not passed.
The prosecution charged offences under the general criminal law provisions on forgery and use of a forged document.
The cooperative-society offence could cover conduct and persons beyond forgery committed with the specific intent required by the general forgery provisions.
issues.conclusion: The cooperative-society offence and the general forgery offences were distinct, and the cooperative-society provision did not repeal the general forgery offences pro tanto.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 463 and 464 of the Indian Penal Code require the specified dishonest or fraudulent making or alteration of a document and the relevant intention or knowledge; the connected forgery and use offences include sections 465 and 471. The cooperative-society offence could apply without the same intention and could extend to persons merely privy to listed acts, as well as to acts such as destruction or secreting of records. Overlap between offences does not establish repeal where their elements and scope differ and they can operate together. The Court applied Om Prakash Gupta v. State of Uttar Pradesh and T. S. Balliah v. T. S. Rengachari.

predicates.criminal_case_for_cooperative_society_re: A criminal case concerns alleged falsification of records belonging to a cooperative society.
predicates.cooperative_offence_does_not_require_gen: The offence applicable to falsification of cooperative-society records does not require the dishonest or fraudulent intent required for general forgery.
predicates.cooperative_offence_covers_additional_ac: The offence applicable to cooperative-society records reaches acts or persons beyond those covered by general forgery offences.

issues.definition: Where a criminal case concerns falsification of cooperative-society records and the cooperative-society offence differs in intent or scope, the general forgery offences remain in force.

issues.legal_issue: Prosecution under the general criminal law for forgery of cooperative-society records does not require the Registrar’s sanction where the prosecution is not brought under the cooperative-society offence.
material_facts: The complaint charged the accused with general criminal law offences for allegedly forging and using the society’s minutes.
The accused objected that prosecution required the Registrar’s prior sanction under the cooperative-society legislation.
The prosecution was brought under the general criminal law provisions, not under the cooperative-society offence.
issues.conclusion: The Registrar’s sanction was not necessary for the prosecution, and the Magistrate could take cognizance of the complaint without it.
issues.legal_principle: The sanction requirement in section 148(3) of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act did not apply to a prosecution brought under the Indian Penal Code rather than for an offence under the cooperative-society legislation. Sections 146(p) and 148(3) of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, read with sections 463, 465 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, do not make the Registrar’s sanction a condition for prosecution of the distinct general criminal law offences. The Court relied on Om Prakash Gupta v. State of Uttar Pradesh and T. S. Balliah v. T. S. Rengachari.

predicates.prosecution_under_cooperative_society_of: The prosecution is brought for an offence specifically created by the law governing cooperative societies.

issues.definition: If alleged falsification of cooperative-society records is prosecuted under general forgery law rather than under the cooperative-society offence, the Registrar’s sanction is not required.
